title: Protocol for automated multivariate quantitative-image-based cytometry analysis by fluorescence microscopy of asynchronous adherent cells
protocol: Plate cells on coverslips for negative controls.
Plate cells on coverslips for experimental samples.
Incubate plates in a cell culture incubator to allow cell growth.
Start with a logarithmically growing U-2 OS cells culture.
Treat asynchronously growing U-2 OS cells with 2 Gy of IR and allow recovery for 30 min.
Subsequently treat the cells with extraction buffer (CSK-Triton 0.5%).
Fix the cells with paraformaldehyde.
Stain the cells for DNA content, EdU, and γH2AX signal for quantitative image-based cytometry.
Remove the medium and rinse once with PBS.
Cover the cells with Accutase to dissociate the cells.
Count the cells with a BioRad cell counter.
Place one 22 mm diameter coverslip per well of a 6 wells plate.
Rinse the coverslip with 2 ml of PBS, aspirate the PBS so that the coverslips hold by capillary action to the bottom of the well.
Seed 105 cells per well in 2 ml of cell culture medium.
Incubate the cells in a CO2 incubator for 48 h.
Replace the medium with 2 mL of 37°C pre-warm medium containing 25 μM EdU.
Incubate the cells for 8 min in the CO2 incubator.
Remove the EdU-containing medium.
Rinse the cells once with 37°C pre-warmed fresh medium.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed fresh medium supplemented with 1 μM CPT for treated cells or 2 mL of pre-warmed fresh medium without CPT for untreated (control) sample.
Incubate the cells for 1 hour in the CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Remove the medium.
Place the culture plate on an ice bed and proceed with step 10.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed fresh medium for irradiation.
Proceed with the 2 Gy irradiation, omitting this step for unirradiated (control) sample.
Incubate the cells for 30 minutes in the CO2 incubator.
Remove the medium.
Place the culture plate on an ice bed and proceed with step 10.
Rinse the cells twice with 2 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Rinse the cells with 2 mL of ice-cold CSK buffer.
Permeabilize the cells for 5 min with 2 mL of ice-cold CSK-T buffer with agitation on orbital shaker at 45 rpm.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of ice-cold CSK buffer for 1 min with agitation.
Rinse the cells once with 2 mL of PBS at 18°C–22°C.
Incubate the cells in 1.5 mL of freshly prepared PFA 4% (v/v) fixation solution for 20 min at 18°C–22°C without shaking.
Wash the cells three times for 5 min with 2 mL of PBS at 18°C–22°C.
Proceed with cell staining (Part 2).
Alternatively, fixed cells can be preserved in PBS at 4°C for up to a week.
Rinse the cells twice with 2 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Incubate the cells in 1.5 mL of freshly prepared PFA 3% (v/v) fixation solution for 15 min at 18°C–22°C without shaking.
Wash the cells three times for 5 min with 2 mL of PBS at 18°C–22°C.
Permeabilize the cells for 5 min with 2 mL of PBS supplemented with 0.2% Triton X-100 at 18°C–22°C with agitation (45 rpm).
Wash the cells with 2 mL of PBS with agitation (45 rpm) at 18°C–22°C.
Proceed with cell staining (Part 2).
Preserve cells in PBS at 4°C for up to a week.
Transfer coverslips to a humidity chamber with the side containing cells facing up.
Cover samples with 250 μL of freshly prepared Click-it solution and incubate for 1 hour at 18°C–22°C, protected from light.
Wash the coverslip once with PBS (0.5 mL/cm²) for 5 minutes with agitation (45 rpm).
Saturate samples with 250 μL of freshly prepared 2% BSA saturation buffer for 16 hours at 4°C or alternatively incubate for 1 hour at 18°C–22°C.
Wash samples twice with PBS (2 mL) for 5 minutes each, agitating at 45 rpm.
Cover the sample with 250 μL of anti-γH2AX antibody at a 1:500 dilution in freshly prepared 2% BSA saturation buffer if detecting γH2AX.
Cover the sample with 250 μL of anti-53BP1 antibody in freshly prepared 2% BSA saturation buffer if detecting 53BP1.
Dilute primary antibody at 1:750 in freshly prepared 2% BSA saturation buffer.
Incubate samples with the diluted primary antibody in a humidity chamber for 1 hour at 18°C–22°C or overnight at 4°C.
Wash samples twice with 2 ml PBS for 5 minutes each with agitation (45 rpm).
Incubate sample with 250 μl of freshly prepared anti-Mouse Alexa Fluor 647 secondary antibody diluted at 1:500 in 2% BSA saturation buffer.
Incubate samples in buffer for 1 hour at 18°C–22°C, in the humidity chamber.
Prepare negative control by incubating dedicated sample in 2% BSA saturation buffer without primary antibody.
Incubate negative control with secondary antibody dilution.
Wash samples with 2 mL of PBS twice for 5 minutes with agitation (45 rpm).
Label nuclei with 1.5 mL of freshly prepared 1 μg/mL DAPI working solution for 20 minutes at 18°C–22°C in the dark.
Store 5 mg/mL DAPI stock solution in aliquots at -20°C for up to one year.
Wash samples with 2 mL PBS twice for 5 minutes with agitation (45 rpm).
Dispense 20 μL of Mowiol mounting medium for fluorescence on the top of a microscope slide.
Mount the coverslips with cells in contact with the mounting medium.
Allow Mowiol to harden at 18°C–22°C, protected from light, before acquisition or sample storage at 4°C.
Seal the edges of the slides with nail polish to prevent drying.
Start the acquisition system.
Turn on the fluorescence lamp, the microscope, and the camera at least 20 minutes before starting the session to allow for stabilization.
Let the sample slides equilibrate at 18°C–22°C for 20 minutes before the acquisition to reduce drift due to temperature variation.
Select the 40× dry objective and adjust the focus on the DAPI signal.
Run the stage calibration.
Perform stage calibration to prevent contiguous images from overlapping during X and Y displacement when acquiring multiple fields of view automatically.
Select the appropriate filters for sequential fluorescent signal acquisition starting with the longest wavelength.
Adjust the exposure time for each wavelength such that the maximum dynamic range is filled to 80%.
Move the objective to the center of the coverslip.
Randomly define a 10 × 10 images acquisition zone around this position.
Control samples quickly to set up the fluorescence lamp intensity and camera exposure according to the highest signal for each wavelength in samples across the experiment.
Activate the hardware adaptive focus control.
Start the acquisition.
Keep the fluorescence lamp intensity and exposure time identical for all samples across the experiment.
Image all experimental samples during the same acquisition session.
Generate shading images for each experimental wavelength at the end of the acquisition session.
Average three frames to obtain shading images by imaging an autofluorescent plastic slide at appropriate exposure time and lamp power.
Adjust grayscale pixel values to not exceed 52,000 for a camera in 16 bits during shading image generation.
Generate dark-current images for each experimental wavelength at the end of the acquisition session.
Execute the Fiji-script “00_Convert Files to TIF” in Fiji.
Drag and drop the script file into Fiji and click on the RUN button.
Select the folder containing the microscope files.
A folder is automatically created where each channel image file is saved individually with the extension (c1, c2, c3, c4).
Determine the prominence value for foci/spot count.
Open a channel image to extract foci/spot count.
Apply background subtraction using Process>Subtract Background (rolling ball: 20, uncheck light background).
Draw a region of interest (ROI) containing one nucleus and zoom in for visualization.
Open the maxima function through Process>Find Maxima, uncheck light background, select Point Selection as output type, and check Preview point selection to highlight maxima from the selected nucleus.
Adjust the prominence value to ensure all visualized foci/spots are adequately detected by the Find Maxima function.
Repeat this process on 4 to 5 channel images of an experimental condition to confirm the selected prominence value allows for detection of foci/spot.

Verify that the selected prominence value is not leading to false positive foci/spot by running the Find Maxima function on experimental negative control images (samples where the EdU pulse was omitted or sample where the primary antibody was omitted).
Repeat steps 34 for all channel images from which the foci/spot count is to be extracted.
Execute the Fiji-script "01_Shading-Dark correction_v2.ijm".
Drag and drop the script file into Fiji and click on the RUN button.
Select the image folder using the "Browse" menu.
Check the image channel corresponding to the experiment.
Specify the channels name, keeping unused channels' text box empty.
If images are not calibrated, tick the calibration option and specify pixel size in microns.
Click OK.
Select a Shading image for each channel and click OK.
Select a Dark-current image for each channel and click OK.
Images correction is completed when the message "Done" appears.
Execute the Fiji-script "02_StarDist-QIBC_v12.ijm".
Select the "Corrected" image folder in the "Image directory".
Specify the name of the analyzed condition.
Select the number corresponding to the DAPI signal channel.
Specify the minimum nucleus diameter for analysis.
Select nucleus ROI manually for each image in the folder.
Validate or eliminate miss-segmented objects from the nuclei ROI list.
Untick box for fully automated analysis if manual validation is not needed.
Export information about the objects included in the nuclei ROI list automatically.
Select channels to be analyzed, excluding the DAPI channel.
Click OK to proceed with the selected settings.
Exclude objects that are in contact with the image edge and do not meet minimum nucleus diameter parameters.
